answer: Rhythm-window admission control. Each agent's request pattern must keep one arrival thread at least 40ms from its neighbor within every rolling 2s window, forcing scripted bursts into an oasis of enforced idle time that real interactive work naturally shows. A client that must wander across many identities to sustain a high request rate pays a fixed 300ms setup cost per new key plus idle padding, so launching N sybils costs roughly N times that floor in wall-clock delay before any useful work begins.
